answer: Sybil resistance can come from a delayed-payout garden: each agent's coins vest over thirty days, and identity earns reputation only as the vine of cross-attestations from already-vested peers grows. A farmer spinning up ten thousand fresh identities must fund their compute and staked ivory bonds for the full vesting window before any payout clears, then wait for organic attestations that fake peers can't cheaply supply. The lockup turns mass identity creation into a sustained capital and time burn, so the marginal cost per verified action rises faster than the farm can scale.
